full_judgment:
8. On 11.11.90, accused preferred appeal against the order of conviction before the learned Sessions Judge, Sylhet in Criminal Appeal No. 15(IV) of 1990, and appellant filed an application under Section 5 of the Limitation Act, for condonation of delay in filing the appeal. The learned Sessions Judge, by his judgment and order dated 15.11.90, held the appeal to be barred by time and on that finding he summarily rejected the appeal without considering other points urged before him. 

 15. The attention of the learned Sessions Judge was not attracted to this aspect of the matter and so he did not have the occasion to consider this aspect. He simply concentrated his attention on the point of limitation and being of the view that appeal is hit by limitation, he summarily rejected it without considering the legality or otherwise of the sentence. The sentence passed by the Upazila Magistrate in the instant case has been found to be without jurisdiction and as such hit by illegality. Therefore, sentence cannot be sustained in law. In the result the judgment passed by learned Seasons judge, Sylhet as well as the order of conviction passed 6y the learned Upazila Magistrate, Balaganj, in G.R. Case No. 176 of 1983 are hereby set aside and the accused petitioner Khalilur Rahman be acquitted and set at liberty forthwith if not wanted in connection with any other case.
